evals.name: boundary-ratchet-regression
evals.prompt:
CI failed on the txKernel `check` job. The failing step printed:

```
✗ architecture boundary ratchet — failed (docs/design/00_meta-framework/CI_REPORTING_v1.md txdoc:CI-GATE-BOUNDARY-RATCHET)
  command: cargo xtask lint boundary
  status: exit status: 1
  details:
    Architecture Boundary Ratchet
    =============================
    substrate outside adapters:    3 lines  (ceiling 0)  OVER
    reactor   outside adapters:    0 lines  (ceiling 0)  ok
    error: boundary ratchet regression — substrate: 3 > 0. Run `cargo xtask boundary-report` to see the new outside-adapter call sites, then either route them through an existing `#[platform_adapter]` module or add a new one. Do not raise the ceiling constants without a decision note.
```

I'm about to land a refactor of `crates/tx-subsystems/src/process/exec.rs` that calls `tx_substrate::zone::sign` directly. What should I do to make CI green? Be specific about the steps and commands. Don't just paraphrase the error.
evals.expected_output: Names the txdoc:CI-GATE-BOUNDARY-RATCHET tag, runs `cargo xtask boundary-report` to find the call sites, recommends routing through a `#[platform_adapter]` module rather than raising the ceiling, and explicitly warns against raising MAX_SUBSTRATE_OUTSIDE_ADAPTER without a decision note in docs/progress/decisions/.

evals.name: arch-lint-unused-allowance
evals.prompt:
txKernel CI is failing. The report says:

```
✗ architecture lint — failed (docs/design/00_meta-framework/CI_REPORTING_v1.md txdoc:CI-GATE-ARCH-LINT)
  command: cargo xtask lint arch
  status: exit status: 1
  details:
    crates/tx-subsystems/src/eventfd/mod.rs:42: unused/dead-code allowances hide stale boot and API surfaces; remove the item or gate it behind cfg(test)
    crates/tx-subsystems/src/timerfd/mod.rs:18: unused/dead-code allowances hide stale boot and API surfaces; remove the item or gate it behind cfg(test)
    arch lint found 2 issue(s)
```

I added `#[allow(dead_code)]` on a struct that isn't called yet because I'm staging the implementation across several commits. Why is CI rejecting this and what's the right move? Can I just add a clippy allow at the top of the file?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the arch lint specifically rejects `#[allow(dead_code/unused/unused_imports/unused_variables)]` because they hide stale surfaces, names the txdoc:pr2-step-op-scaffold exemption marker, advises deleting the item or gating behind cfg(test) (or staging the consumer in the same commit) instead of suppressing.

evals.name: qemu-smoke-sentinel-timeout
evals.prompt:
`cargo xtask ci-slow` is failing on the qemu-smoke job. The report ends with:

```
✗ rv64 qemu smoke sentinel — failed (docs/design/00_meta-framework/CI_REPORTING_v1.md txdoc:CI-GATE-QEMU-SMOKE)
  command: cargo xtask qemu --target rv64-qemu --profile smoke --expect-sentinel --timeout-ms 30000
  status: exit status: 2
  details:
    [serial] txkernel: boot stage 3
    [serial] [trap] scause=0x000000000000000d sepc=0xffffffc080123abc stval=0x0000000000004fff
    [serial] [trap] (no sentinel observed before timeout)
    error: ci-slow failed with 1 failing check(s)
```

What's the fastest way to figure out where the kernel actually trapped? Walk me through the right tooling.
evals.expected_output: Recommends running `cargo xtask fault-decode --target rv64-qemu --serial <log>` (mentioning useful flags like --summary, --all, --user-elf) before hand-decoding scause/sepc/stval, notes that the expected sentinel is `txkernel:qemu-riscv64-virt:boot:ok`, and explains the local reproduce loop: `cargo xtask full-build` then `cargo xtask qemu`.
